guideline: Apply the guide to new text and to text you're already changing. Don't open a document only to restyle it.
note: Process guidance.

guideline: Two tables under Terminology are templates: your product names and the third-party brands you write about.
note: The guide's tables are unfilled templates. Only the brand names the guide itself prints are checked. Add your own product names and brands to the brand-casing rule.

guideline: Clear, direct, warm, honest.
note: Tone and accuracy need a reader.

section: Voice > Adjust the tone to the moment
guideline: Tone table: first use, routine task, errors, data loss, security, milestones.
Never joke in an error message.
note: Humor isn't pattern-matchable.

guideline: Twelve rules that cover most edits.
note: Lead with the point, serial comma, and naming UI labels exactly are listed under their own sections.

guideline: Don't change any fact, number, date, version, name, step, sequence, condition, scope, or claim.
note: The tool never edits, so this is satisfied by design. Fidelity between drafts needs a reader.

section: Editing someone else's text > Edit or flag
guideline: An acronym with no expansion anywhere in the source: flag it.
note: Common acronyms are skipped by a built-in list.

section: Editing someone else's text > Edit or flag
guideline: Something that looks like a real key, password, or customer record in a sample: flag it.
note: Prose only. Code blocks aren't checked.

section: Editing someone else's text > When rules conflict
guideline: A fact in the source is never changed. An existing UI label is copied exactly.
Table of long phrases and their short forms.
note: "A number of" is a suggestion because the guide also uses it as a valid phrase in the Agreement section.

section: Sentences > Say what is, not what isn't
guideline: Use a positive statement when it means exactly the same thing.
note: Whether a negative is a fact needs a reader. The contraction suggestion covers "does not" and similar forms only as a wording hint.

section: Sentences > Flag vague claims, don't sharpen them
guideline: Updates in near real time. Shows key events. Scales to meet enterprise needs.
note: Only the guide's example phrases and close variants.

guideline: Most adjectives and adverbs are padding.
note: Only the words in the word list are checked.

guideline: Items in a list, headings at one level, and steps take the same grammatical form.
note: Grammatical form isn't reliably detectable with patterns.

section: Sentences > Keep modifiers next to what they modify
guideline: Put the modifier next to the word you mean. Dangling modifiers.
Put the key word first in a heading, a label, a list item, and the first sentence.
note: Only announcing sentences are caught.

guideline: Opens, not will open.
note: Only "<product noun> will <verb>" is flagged. Statements about release timing are excluded.

guideline: Convert passive to active only when the actor is named or obvious.
note: Only passives with an explicit "by" actor are flagged, since those are the ones the guide says to convert.

section: Sentences > Write facts as statements and steps as commands
guideline: Don't phrase advice as a wish.
note: "It is recommended" and "we recommend" forms.

guideline: Use common contractions. Avoid unusual ones and contractions of nouns.
note: Noun contractions ("the project's been") aren't distinguishable from possessives by pattern. Legal text is a stated exception the tool can't recognize.

guideline: use over utilize, help over facilitate, through over via.
An -ing heading can mean two things.
note: Ambiguity needs a reader.

section: Sentences > Keep chains of prepositions short
guideline: More than two prepositional phrases in a row are hard to follow.
note: Counting prepositional phrases needs parsing the tool doesn't do.

guideline: One topic per paragraph. Don't explain twice.
note: Length is a proxy only. 150 words is this tool's threshold.

section: Talking to the reader > Write to you
guideline: Address the reader as you. Don't write the user. Cut you can when the sentence works without it.
note: Category uses such as "user account" are excluded by a list of following nouns.

section: Talking to the reader > Name everyone else by role
guideline: Everyone else gets a role name, not a pronoun.

section: Talking to the reader > Use we only when the company is speaking
guideline: Don't use we to give advice.
note: Other uses of "we" are left alone, since a privacy notice or outage update is a valid use.

section: Talking to the reader > I, me, and my
guideline: In documentation, never use first person singular. Don't mix my and your on the same screen.
note: Only "I" followed by a common verb is flagged, because UI labels such as "Keep me signed in" are allowed.

section: Talking to the reader > Text the product generated
guideline: Use past tense and make clear that a judgment was applied.
Collective nouns, and, or, a number of.
note: Subject-verb agreement needs parsing.

guideline: Use singular they for a person whose gender isn't known.
APIs not API's. 2020s. Don't write (s). Don't make a product name possessive. Its versus it's.
note: Product name possessives need the product name table, which is a template in the guide.

guideline: Sentence case for headings, titles, labels, buttons, menu items, list items. Capitalize the first word after a colon in a heading.
note: Title case is detected when two or more words after the first are capitalized and aren't acronyms. Proper nouns can't be told from title case, so it's a warning. UI labels and buttons aren't identifiable in Markdown.

section: Capitalization > Proper nouns and common nouns
guideline: Most technology terms are common nouns: cloud computing, machine learning, open source, single sign-on.
note: Only the terms the guide lists. Dashboard and workspace are excluded because they are often UI labels.

guideline: Copy UI labels from the source. Generic UI elements lowercase. No all caps for emphasis. No internal capitals. Spelled-out acronyms lowercase. Slashes. Defined terms. Lowercase identifiers.
note: Label copying, defined terms, and identifiers at sentence start are human review.

section: Capitalization > When title case is required
guideline: Title case rules for published works, events, job titles, and product names.
note: The tool can't know which headings are titles of published works.

guideline: Use the full, approved product name on first mention. Retire aliases.
note: The product name table is a template with a fictional row. Add real names to the brand-casing rule or a new term-replace rule.

guideline: Pick AI assistant or virtual assistant and don't alternate among assistant, bot, chatbot, and agent.
note: Fires once per term when two or more of the generic terms appear in one document.

guideline: Capitalize a defined term the same way every time. Keep undefined terms lowercase.
note: The tool doesn't know which terms a document defines.

section: Terminology > Product terms must name real things
guideline: A term that exists only in a design document sends readers looking for a screen that isn't there.
Use the owner's exact casing. Symbols per the brand table. Attribution line. Don't use a brand as a verb.
note: Symbol placement and the attribution line depend on the brand table, which the guide leaves unchecked. Human review.

guideline: Spell out on first use. Skip for well-known acronyms. Not in a heading. Lowercase the spelled-out form. A or an by sound. No possessive. Avoid Latin abbreviations.
note: "Spell out your own product names" and "skip the acronym for a term you use once" are human review.

guideline: Write / Instead of table.
note: The "keep, or flag" row (may, might, could, typically, usually, up to, at least) creates no rule, since those words are facts more often than not.

section: Writing about product behavior > Describe only what ships today
guideline: Don't describe planned features, roadmap items, or capabilities behind a setting the reader can't turn on.
note: Only phrases such as "coming soon" and "in a future release".

section: Writing about product behavior > Leave out internal implementation details
guideline: Leave out service names, table names, polling intervals, cache behavior.
note: Whether a detail is internal or a reader-facing setting needs the author.

section: Writing about product behavior > Describe failure concretely
guideline: Say what the reader will see, why, and what to do next.

section: Writing about product behavior > Don't promise outcomes
guideline: Avoid always, never, guarantees, ensures, and eliminates when you describe what a model does.
note: "Eliminates" is covered by the combat rule so the two rules don't both fire on it. "Always" and "never" are flagged only before a product verb.

section: Writing about product behavior > Keep supported behavior in
guideline: Trimming claims doesn't mean trimming facts.

section: UI text > Quick check for any string
guideline: Sentence case, period rules, shortest version, no please, sorry, or oops.
note: Markdown has no way to mark a string as a UI label, so label-specific period rules are human review.

section: UI text > Capitalization and punctuation in UI
guideline: No period, colon, or ellipsis on a label. No exclamation points.
note: Heading rules stand in for label rules, since labels aren't identifiable in Markdown.

guideline: Lead with the verb. Three words at most. Never OK to confirm.
note: Buttons aren't identifiable in Markdown.

guideline: Never "Are you sure?" or "Warning!" Two actions at most. Never OK.
note: Button counts are human review.

guideline: Say what happened, why, and what to do. One message per known cause. No please, sorry, oops, or unfortunately.
note: Whether an error has a next step is human review.

guideline: Label as a noun phrase with no colon. Placeholder is an example. Mark the rarer kind of field.
note: Form fields aren't identifiable in Markdown.

guideline: A phrase, not a paragraph. No period unless two sentences.
One line. One action at most. No links inside the text.
Past tense, one line, no exclamation point.
Say why there's nothing here, then what to do.
Never "click here", never "learn more" on its own.
Icon labels. Alt text. Don't rely on color alone. Don't rely on position.
note: Color-only references ("the red status") are human review.

guideline: Open, close, go to, select, clear, enter, press, turn on. Avoid click and tap. In a dialog, on a tab.

section: UI text > Naming a label inside a UI sentence
guideline: Match the label exactly. Don't bold it in UI text.
note: The tool can't tell UI strings from documentation.

section: UI text > First person in UI
guideline: Me and my are fine where the reader is the speaker. Don't mix my and your on one screen.

section: UI text > Third-party brands in UI
guideline: Symbol depends on the surface.
Short strings. No runtime concatenation. No hard-coded formats. Leave tokens as written.
Bold the label and copy it exactly. Bold for UI labels and run-in headings only, never for emphasis. Drop a trailing colon or ellipsis.
note: Bold for emphasis can't be told from a bold label by pattern.

guideline: Menu paths, code style, placeholders, keys and shortcuts, new terms in italic, quoted error text, file formats in capitals.
note: Code style for commands and placeholders is human review.

guideline: Sentence case. One title. Don't skip levels. Front-load. Verb for tasks. Parallel. Don't stack. No acronyms. No ampersands. No period.
note: Front-loading, verb-first task headings, and parallelism are human review.

guideline: Prerequisites first. Number the steps. One action per step. Start with a verb. Optional: prefix. Full sentences with a period. About seven steps. Single step uses a bullet.
note: One action per step and verb-first steps are human review. The long-procedure check allows nine steps because the guide says "about seven".

guideline: Bulleted for no order, numbered for a sequence. Two to seven items. Parallel. Capital first letter. Periods only for full sentences. No semicolons, commas, or conjunctions at the ends.
note: Parallelism and period-for-full-sentences need a reader.

section: Documentation > Lists > Use bullets for dense status lists
guideline: Break a paragraph of comma-separated states into a term list.
Row identifier in the leftmost column. Sentence case in cells. Specific headers. Never a blank cell. Introduce with a sentence ending in a period.
note: Header specificity is human review.

guideline: Use sparingly. Don't stack callouts. No step inside one.
note: Callout syntax varies between Markdown flavors.

guideline: Link text names the destination. Don't link the same destination twice in a section. Don't point with above or below.
Crop. Text must work without the screenshot. Fictional data. Alt text that says what it shows, not "Image of". Update stale screenshots.
note: Image content is not inspected.

guideline: One entry per noticeable change. Fixed headings. Start with what changed. Name the version and date. No thanks or apology.
note: Heading order and version naming are human review.

guideline: HTTP method in capitals, path in code style. Present-tense verb. Parameter tables. Complete examples. Document every error.
note: Everything else is human review.

guideline: Samples run. Placeholders marked. No real keys or customer records. Show expected output.
note: Code blocks are not checked, so these fire only on prose.

guideline: "The table below shows...", "This section explains...", "In today's fast-paced digital world...", "It is important to note that...", closing paragraphs that restate.
note: Restating closing paragraphs are human review.

guideline: Words below 10 in prose, numerals from 10. Numerals in UI and tables. Numerals throughout when mixed. Never a numeral at sentence start. Numerals for measurements. Time of day. Percent.
note: List items are treated as prose. Numbers followed by a unit, a unit word, or preceded by words such as step, version, or port are exempt.

guideline: Comma from four digits. Not in years, versions, ports, or identifiers.
note: Four-digit numbers are skipped because most are years. Five or more digits are suggested only.

guideline: Space between number and unit. No space before %. Plural unit unless exactly 1.
note: Plural units are human review.

guideline: Spell out the month. No ordinals. ISO in data. Time zone. Month or quarter, not season.
note: Time zones are human review.

guideline: From 5 through 50 in prose. En dash with no spaces in tables. To for times. No from before an en dash.
1.2 million in prose. K, M, B in tight UI.
Leading zero. Minus sign. Ordinals spelled out, no firstly. Versions as published. Fictional phone numbers.
note: A hyphen used as a minus sign can't be told from a range or a compound. Phone numbers are human review.

guideline: Period on every full sentence. One space after. No period on headings, labels, or fragment list items.
note: Which list items are full sentences needs a reader.

guideline: Serial comma. Comma after an introductory phrase. Comma before and, but, so joining sentences. No comma between two verbs sharing a subject.
note: A reliable serial-comma check needs to know where a series starts, which patterns get wrong often enough to be noise. Assumption: left to human review rather than shipping a noisy rule.

guideline: Colon to introduce a list. Not to attach an explanation. Lowercase after a colon in a sentence. Never at the end of a heading or label.
note: Colons that attach explanations are human review.

guideline: Don't use them.
note: HTML entities such as & are excluded.

guideline: No em dash. En dash for ranges with no spaces. Minus sign for negatives.
note: A double hyphen is treated as an em dash. Minus signs are human review.

guideline: Compound modifiers before a noun. No hyphen after -ly. Most prefixes closed. Spell out both parts. Email.
note: Compound modifiers before a noun need a parser.

guideline: 's for singular possessives. No apostrophe plurals. No product name possessives.
note: Product names come from the unfilled table.

guideline: Straight quotes. Periods and commas inside, except literal values. Single quotes only inside quotes. Not for emphasis.
note: Quotes for emphasis are human review.

guideline: For an aside only. Don't nest. Period inside only when the whole sentence is in parentheses.
Not at the end of a label. Progress messages can end with one.
note: Headings stand in for labels.

section: Punctuation > Exclamation points and question marks
guideline: No exclamation points. Questions for decisions.
Only for fixed pairs. Not for or. Forward slashes in cross-platform paths.
note: Only "and/or" and pairs of common product nouns are flagged, to avoid firing on paths and fixed pairs.

guideline: Use and.
Punctuation takes the style of the sentence, not the label.

section: Inclusive language > Pronouns in generic references
guideline: No he, she for a generic person. Never he/she or s/he.
Table.

section: Inclusive language > Terms that carry bias
guideline: Table.
note: "Master" alone is not flagged, since it has many non-biased uses. "Hang" is flagged only after a product noun.

section: Inclusive language > Combat and violence metaphors
guideline: Table. Also avoid strike and troops.
note: "Strike" is not flagged because it has too many ordinary uses. "Combat" and "fight" are flagged only before a noun they would attack.

guideline: People first. No wheelchair-bound, stricken with, suffering from. No disability metaphors.
Capitalize names of groups. Lowercase white and multiracial.
note: Casing of these words depends on context the tool can't read.

guideline: Don't use age as shorthand for skill.
Varied names. No Western assumptions. No disputed places. No generalizations. No spirit animal or tribe.
note: Only the two phrases the guide names.

guideline: Products don't think, feel, want, or decide.
One idea per sentence. Keep that. Avoid idioms. Avoid Latin abbreviations. Spell out months. Name the currency. Avoid acronyms that look like words. Keep text out of images.
note: Only the two idioms the guide names are checked.

guideline: Em dashes. Semicolons. Mid-sentence colons. Not just X. Announcing openers. Introducing sentences. Stacked hedges. Filler intensifiers. Moreover and Furthermore. Punchy one-liners. Scattered bold. Restating closers.
note: Mid-sentence colons, punchy one-liners, scattered bold, and restating closers are human review.

guideline: Claims, terminology, machine tells, structure, proofreading, fidelity.
note: Process guidance.

guideline: Spelling, doubled words, agreement, tense drift, dangling modifiers, awkward phrasing, punctuation, capitalization, numbers, links.
note: General spelling, homophones other than its/it's, agreement, and dangling modifiers are human review.

guideline: Keep an instruction to 20 words and a description to 25.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Replaces the base 30-word suggestion. Thresholds are this project's own numbers.

guideline: Keep a paragraph to six sentences or fewer.
note: Strict-plain profile only.

section: Strict-plain overlay > One instruction per sentence
guideline: Give one instruction in each sentence.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Looks for and, then or a semicolon followed by a second command.

guideline: Put the condition before the instruction.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Looks for if, when or unless after a command.

guideline: Use the simple present or simple past; avoid perfect and progressive forms.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Modal hedges (may have, must have) and -ing adjectives (missing, pending) are left alone.

section: Strict-plain overlay > Active voice in instructions
guideline: In an instruction, say who does what.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Procedure blocks and instruction sentences only; states such as 'is installed' and passives with 'by' (base rule) are left alone.

guideline: Use must, we recommend, you can or can instead of should and may.
note: Strict-plain profile only. 'Should' is an error and 'may' a warning, by owner decision. 'May' followed by a number (a date) is left alone.

guideline: Write the full form instead of a contraction.
note: Strict-plain profile only, as an error. Replaces the base advice to use contractions; the base profile keeps that advice.

section: Strict-plain overlay > One term per concept
guideline: Use the glossary's preferred word for each term.
note: Strict-plain profile only. Terms come from glossary/starter.csv and the project glossary named in stylebound.config.json. The synonym-group rule one-term-per-concept was dropped after the precision gate (docs/RULES-DROPPED.html).
